facts.statement: Erlikosaurus was named and described by Barsbold and Perle in 1980.
facts.quote: authority: Barsbold & Perle, 1980

facts.statement: Fossils of Erlikosaurus were discovered in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia in 1972.
facts.quote: The fossils, a skull and some post-cranial fragments, were found in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia in 1972

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Erlikosaurus (meaning "Erlik's lizard") is a genus of therizinosaurid that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus lived approximately 96 to 89 million years ago.
facts.quote: dating to around 96 and 89 million years ago

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Erlikosaurus was found at the Bayshin Tsav locality within the Bayan Shireh Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MPC-D 100/111, was found in layers from the Bayshin Tsav locality on the Bayan Shireh Formation

facts.statement: The Erlikosaurus fossils were found during a Soviet-Mongolian expedition in the Ömnögovi Province in 1972.
facts.quote: These findings were made during a Soviet-Mongolian expedition in the Ömnögovi Province in 1972

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus possessed a well-developed beak and toothed jaws adapted for a herbivorous diet.
facts.quote: It had a well-developed beak at the snout tip and toothed jaws that were used for its herbivorous diet

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus had four toes on its feet, with the first toe articulated to the ankle.
facts.quote: The feet ended in four toes with the first one articulated to the ankle

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus had a large gut, strong arms with elongated claws, and a pelvis directed backwards.
facts.quote: Like other therizinosaurids, Erlikosaurus had a large gut for food processing, strong arms ending in elongated claws, and a backwards directed pelvis

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus is known for having the most complete skull among therizinosaurids from the Bayan Shireh Formation.
facts.quote: It represents the second therizinosaur taxon from this formation (after Segnosaurus), with the most complete skull among members of this peculiar family of dinosaurs

facts.statement: The name Erlikosaurus combines the Turko-Mongolian demon king Erlik with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name, Erlikosaurus, was taken from that of the demon king Erlik, from Turko-Mongolian mythology and the Greek σαῦρος (sauros, meaning lizard)

facts.statement: The species name andrewsi honors the American paleontologist Roy Chapman Andrews.
facts.quote: The specific name, andrewsi, is in honour to the American paleontologist Roy Chapman Andrews

facts.statement: At the time of its description, Erlikosaurus was the only therizinosaur known to have a complete skull.
facts.quote: At the time of its discovery it was the only known therizinosaur (then called segnosaurs) for which a complete skull had been discovered

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul suggested that Erlikosaurus might be synonymous with Enigmosaurus, a hypothesis disputed by Rinchen Barsbold.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul challenged the validity of this taxon, arguing that Erlikosaurus may be synonymous with Enigmosaurus

facts.statement: Most paleontologists currently consider Enigmosaurus and Erlikosaurus to be separate genera.
facts.quote: Consequently, Enigmosaurus and Erlikosaurus are generally considered separated genera

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Erlikosaurus measures approximately 25 cm in length.
facts.quote: The skull of the holotype specimen length is approximately 25 cm long, indicating a very small individual

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus was a small therizinosaurid estimated to reach about 3.4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Overall, Erlikosaurus was a small-sized therizinosaurid, estimated to have reach about 3.4 m with a more lightly built than the ponderous Segnosaurus

facts.statement: Estimates suggest Erlikosaurus had a body mass ranging between 150 and 250 kg.
facts.quote: they established an overall mass range between 150 and 250 kg

facts.statement: Alternative estimates have proposed a maximum length of 6 meters and a weight of 500 kg for Erlikosaurus.
facts.quote: Alternative estimations have suggested a maximum length of 6 m long, and a more conservative length of 4.5 metres and a weight of 500 kg

facts.statement: Based on related species, it is likely that Erlikosaurus was covered in feathers.
facts.quote: It is known that therizinosaurs were feathered animals based on the preserved feather impressions in specimens of Beipiaosaurus and Jianchangosaurus, so it is likely that Erlikosaurus was feathered as well

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus likely used a leaf-stripping feeding method involving active beak use aided by its neck.
facts.quote: The beak and jaws of Erlikosaurus indicate a leaf-stripping feeding method characterized by the active use of the beak aided by the neck

facts.statement: Differences between Erlikosaurus and the co-existing Segnosaurus suggest they occupied different ecological niches.
facts.quote: Several differences with the sympatric Segnosaurus show that these related genera were niche partitioned

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus had a moderately elongated snout with a premaxilla featuring elongated nasal processes.
facts.quote: The snout is moderately elongated, with a premaxilla featuring elongated nasal processes.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Erlikosaurus was triangular in shape and contained 24 tooth sockets with homodont teeth that had coarse serrations.
facts.quote: The maxilla is triangular in shape and preserves 24 alveoli, the teeth are homodont with coarse serrations.

facts.statement: The dentary of Erlikosaurus was wedge-shaped, elongated, and preserved 31 tooth sockets.
facts.quote: The dentary is wedge-shaped elongated and preserves 31 alveoli.

facts.statement: Restored measurements indicate the skull of Erlikosaurus was 26 cm long and the mandible was about 24 cm.
facts.quote: When restored, the skull measures 26 cm long and the mandible is about 24 cm.

facts.statement: In Erlikosaurus, the olfactory tract was significantly larger than the actual brain.
facts.quote: The olfactory tract being far larger than the actual brain.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that the keratinous beak (rhamphotheca) of Erlikosaurus covered the nasal process of the premaxilla.
facts.quote: Apparently, in Erlikosaurus the rhamphotheca covered the nasal process of the premaxilla.

facts.statement: The preserved left humerus of Erlikosaurus was robust, had an estimated length of 30 cm, and featured an elongated epiphysis and a large deltoidal process.
facts.quote: The humerus shows an elongated epiphyses and a relatively large deltoidal process. It is robust with an estimated length of 30 cm.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul hypothesized that the long, slender claws of Erlikosaurus were used for self-defense.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul surmised that the long, slender claws of the feet were used for self-defence mechanism.

facts.statement: Perle originally assigned Erlikosaurus to the Segnosauridae, a group now known as Therizinosauridae, a classification confirmed by later cladistic analyses.
facts.quote: Erlikosaurus was by Perle assigned to the Segnosauridae, a group today known as the Therizinosauridae, confirmed by later cladistic analyses.

facts.statement: Therizinosaurs like Erlikosaurus were theropods that ate plants and possessed a backward-facing pubis similar to ornithischians.
facts.quote: Therizinosaurs were a strange group of theropods that ate plants instead of meat, and had a backward-facing pubis, like ornithischians.

facts.statement: In 1970, Rozhdestvensky proposed that therizinosaurs were theropods rather than non-dinosaur creatures, a view that was debated before being widely accepted.
facts.quote: However, in 1970, Rozhdestvensky proposed the idea that therizinosaurs (then known as segnosaurs) instead of being non-dinosaur creatures, they were in fact, theropods.

facts.statement: CT scans of the holotype skull revealed that Erlikosaurus had well-developed senses of smell, hearing, and balance.
facts.quote: Analysis of the brain cavity revealed that Erlikosaurus, and quite likely most other therizinosaurids, had well developed senses of smell, hearing, and balance

facts.statement: Bite force measurements showed a range of 43–65 N at the snout tip and 90–134 N at the last maxillary tooth region.
facts.quote: Lautenschlager found the lowest force at the snout tip with 43–65 N, and the highest at the last maxillar tooth region, with 90–134 N

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Erlikosaurus used the tip of its snout to reach for soft foliage or fruits rather than active mastication.
facts.quote: Factors like the presence of a large gut to process vegetation and the lack of damage patterns on the teeth suggest that Erlikosaurus used only the tip of the snout and the premaxillary region to reach for soft foliage or fruits

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that the keratinous beak enhanced skull stability by reducing susceptibility to bending during feeding.
facts.quote: They concluded that keratinous beaks are beneficial to enhance the stability of the skull making it less susceptible to bending and/or deformation during feeding

facts.statement: Finite Element Analysis estimated Erlikosaurus bite force to be between 50 and 121 Newtons.
facts.quote: The resulting bite force for Erlikosaurus was between 50 and 121 N

facts.statement: The Bayan Shireh Formation, where Erlikosaurus was found, dates from approximately 95.9 to 89.6 million years ago (Cenomanian to Santonian stages).
facts.quote: calcite U–Pb measurements estimate the age of the Bayan Shireh Formation from 95.9 ± 6.0 million to 89.6 ± 4.0 million years ago, Cenomanian through Santonian ages

facts.statement: Sediment analysis indicates Erlikosaurus lived in a semi-arid climate featuring wet environments with large meandering rivers and lakes.
facts.quote: Fluvial, lacustrine and caliche-based sedimentation indicates a lesser semi-arid climate, with the presence of wet environments composed of large meanders and lakes

facts.statement: Contemporary theropods in the same formation included Khankhuuluu, Achillobator, and Garudimimus.
facts.quote: Fellow theropods include the tyrannosauroid Khankhuuluu, the large dromaeosaurid Achillobator, and the deinocheirid Garudimimus

facts.statement: Other herbivorous dinosaurs sharing the habitat included Talarurus, Tsagantegia, Amtocephale, Graciliceratops, Gobihadros, and Erketu.
facts.quote: Other herbivorous dinosaurs are represented by the ankylosaurs Talarurus and Tsagantegia, small marginocephalians Amtocephale and Graciliceratops, the hadrosauroid Gobihadros, and the sauropod Erketu

facts.statement: The genus Erlikosaurus was described by Barsbold and Perle in 1980.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Erlikosaurus (genus), Barsbold and Perle 1980

facts.quote: Parent group: Therizinosauria

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus lived from the Turonian to the Santonian stages, between 93.9 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Santonian (93.9 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus lived alongside the larger therizinosaurid Segnosaurus in the Bayan Shireh Formation.
facts.quote: Erlikosaurus lived alongside a larger species of therizinosaurid in the Bayan Shireh Formation, Segnosaurus.

facts.statement: Erlikosaurus possessed very symmetrical teeth with moderate denticles.
facts.quote: On the contrary, the latter has very symmetrical teeth with moderate denticles.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Erlikosaurus was aided by a down-turned tip of the lower jaws, symphyseal regions, and stress-mitigating beaks.
facts.quote: In contrast, Erlikosaurus and Segnosaurus were aided by the down-turned tip of the lower jaws and symphyseal (bone union) regions, and probably also by stress and strain-mitigating beaks.
